Agent Attention — Which One Is Asking?

Features·seedling·proposed·JUL 21, 2026

When an agent asks a question, kolu shows a "1" on the host tab and a faint dot on the dock entry — but you still have to hunt for which agent needs you, and the "asking" dot is the quietest mark in the palette. This note ships two small fixes that use state the client already holds, and scopes the one that doesn't (surfacing the question text) as a separate, brittler pass.

Contents

  • AD1 — the awaiting pill becomes a jump button
  • AD2 — a genuinely-blocked agent gets its own pip
  • Option 3 — surfacing the question text — is deliberately out of scope
  • What ships here

When an agent stops to ask you something — a Claude Code AskUserQuestion, an ExitPlanMode — kolu already notices. The host tab grows a small amber count (a “1”), and the agent’s dock entry gets an orange mark. So the signal exists. The problem is that the signal is weak on both ends of the question you actually ask:

  • Which agent is asking? The host-tab pill tells you how many terminals are waiting, never which. To find the one blocked on you, you scan the dock for the orange mark by eye.
  • Is this even important? The “asking” mark on the dock entry is the faintest pip in the whole palette — a 6px dot at 55% opacity.PIP_BODY.awaiting is w-1.5 h-1.5 rounded-full bg-alert/55 — packages/solid-statepip/src/pipVariant.ts. Meanwhile the unread corner badge (an agent that finished while you looked away — lower stakes) pulses. The loudness hierarchy is inverted.

Both gaps are fixable with facts the client already has on hand — no new wire field, no new sensing. This note ships those two (AD1, AD2), and scopes the third idea (surface the question text) honestly as a bigger, brittler pass we are not taking here.

AD1 — the awaiting pill becomes a jump button

The host’s urgency cell already carries the identities of the waiting terminals, not just a count: { awaitingIds: TerminalId[] }, folded server-side by recomputeUrgency. packages/padi/src/urgency.ts The UI throws that away today — useHostAwaiting projects it straight down to .length. packages/client/src/host/useHostAwaiting.ts

So AD1 is pure wiring:

  • useHostAwaiting returns the ids, not the count. Its three readers (HostChip, HostSwitcherRow, MobileHostChip) switch from awaiting() to awaiting().length for the badge — one character of churn each.
  • The pill turns into a button. HostAwaitingPill gains an optional onActivate; with it, the mark renders as a real <button> instead of a <span>. In HostChip the pill moves out of the role="tab" select button to sit beside it as a sibling — the same shape the remove-✕ already uses — so we never nest a button inside a button.Nested interactive elements (<button> inside <button role="tab">) are invalid HTML and produce unreliable keyboard / screen-reader behaviour. The existing remove-✕ is already a sibling of the tab button inside the host-tab shell for exactly this reason — AD1 follows that precedent.
  • Clicking jumps to the agent. The handler runs setActiveHost(host) (if not already there) then tileStore.activate(id), cycling through awaitingIds on repeated clicks. This is the exact switch-then-activate seam the cross-host notification click already runsuseHostAttention’s notify.onClick router does setActiveHost(decodeHostKey(host)) then focusTerminal(id) — packages/client/src/host/useHostAttention.ts. focusTerminal is the terminal store’s activate, which targets the now-active host after the switch. AD1 reuses this proven path rather than inventing a second one. — so a badge click and a notification click do the same thing, and there is no second focus path to keep in sync.

AD2 — a genuinely-blocked agent gets its own pip

The dim dot is dim on purpose — but the purpose is being over-applied. kolu’s paint fold deliberately collapses two different states into one amber dot: an agent blocked on your answer (awaiting_user) and an agent that just finished its turn (waiting, the post-turn lull). packages/terminal-vocab/src/agentProjection.ts A just-finished agent keeping a quiet lingering glow is correct. The bug is that the agent asking you a question right now whispers at the same volume.

AD2 splits only the loud end back out:

  • A new blocked pip variant in @kolu/solid-statepip — full-opacity, larger, and pulsing, versus the dim lingering awaiting dot which stays exactly as it is.
  • Promoted through the existing agentBucket fence, not a new paint class. agentBucket already distinguishes the two — awaiting_user → "awaiting", waiting → "waiting". packages/terminal-vocab/src/agentProjection.ts So paintDockRow (for the dock rows) and agentPipVariant (for the tile-title pip) each promote agentBucket(state) === "awaiting" to blocked, and everything else folds through the shared paint class unchanged.

Why not just split the shared AgentPaintClass?

Because that is the wrong-sized cut. AgentPaintClass is read by the tile aura, the minimap badge, and the expanded-switcher columns (via AgentBucketKind in dockModel.ts). Adding blocked there forces a new column in the switcher and a louder aura on every canvas tile — surfaces the user never complained about. Keeping blocked dock-local (an added member of DockRowBucket) plus the tile-title pip touches exactly the two surfaces in the complaint and leaves the rest alone. The codebase’s parity invariant — dock row pip ≡ tile-title pip — still holds, because both promote through the same agentBucket check.Pinned by the parity test at packages/client/src/canvas/dock/dockRowRanking.test.ts, which AD2 updates to compare the two computed pip variants (both promoting) rather than the raw pre-promotion paint bucket.

Option 3 — surfacing the question text — is deliberately out of scope

The natural next wish is for the dock entry’s subtitle to show the question itself (“What would you like to work on?”) instead of the stale session title. We scoped it, and it is a genuinely bigger, brittler pass — so it is not in this PR.

The wire plumbing would be cheap: one nullable field on ClaudeCodeInfoSchema rides the whole zod-driven surface for free, and the dock subtitle (rowSubline.ts) is a one-line change. The hard part is that the question text is not anywhere kolu can cleanly read while the question is pending. kolu senses Claude Code state by tailing the session’s JSONL transcript — but the Claude Agent SDK buffers the AskUserQuestion tool-use block off-disk until you answer, so the transcript path (which does have a question decoder) is useless for a live question. packages/integrations/claude-code/src/agent-adapter.ts The only live source is the rendered screen: today the adapter screen-scrapes the dialog’s footer chrome to detect that a prompt is present, capturing no text. packages/integrations/claude-code/src/screen.ts Surfacing the text means parsing the question body out of that screen region — stripping box characters, option lists, and soft-wrapping — a new, version-sensitive parser whose comments already warn the presence regexes drift across Claude Code releases, and which buys only Claude Code (Codex, opencode, grok each render prompts differently).

If we ever do option 3, do it through a hook, not a scraper

A Claude Code PreToolUse hook on AskUserQuestion could hand kolu the exact question text non-brittly. The adapter uses no hooks today, so that is its own new integration mechanism (with a “how does the hook config reach users’ sessions” question attached) — which is precisely why it belongs in a separate note, not bolted onto this one.

What ships here

One PR, two tracks, both grounded in state the client already receives:

Track Change Blast radius
AD1 Awaiting pill → jump button (cycles awaitingIds) useHostAwaiting, HostAwaitingPill, HostChip + the two other pill readers
AD2 blocked pip for a genuinely-asking agent @kolu/solid-statepip, paintDockRow, dock pipVariant, TerminalMeta, one index.css rule

Neither track adds a wire field or a new sensing path — that is the line that keeps them small, and the line option 3 would have crossed.
